variants.headline: Shipbuilding for the colony route
variants.sub: Shipbuilding by the home world has provided a larger vessel or another vessel for the colony route.
variants.body:
The home world has built a larger ship or an additional ship for the colony route. The construction is a transport development, not an announcement of arrival. In assessing {target}, readers should distinguish provision of a vessel from an unreported schedule, cargo or immediate change in supplies.

A ship has been built for the route. Keep the people behind the story in view, and ask the hard questions without inventing answers.

variants.headline: Home world builds for the colonial crossing
variants.sub: A larger ship or one more ship has been built for the colony route.
variants.body:
A ship built for the colony route is a physical commitment to that connection. The home world has provided a larger vessel or another vessel. For {target}, the event invites judgment about transport provision without assuming that construction establishes a particular launch date or frequency of service.

A ship has been built for the route. Keep the people behind the story in view, and ask the hard questions without inventing answers.

variants.headline: Route gains a shipbuilding development
variants.sub: The home world has built a larger ship or an additional ship for the colony route.
variants.body:
The route to the colony is the subject of a shipbuilding development: the home world has built a larger ship or one more ship. Any assessment of {target} should begin there, rather than with a forecast of passengers or goods that the report does not supply.

A ship has been built for the route. Keep the people behind the story in view, and ask the hard questions without inventing answers.
